Yesterday I became aware of the fact that users with negative CCP are severely limited in their ability to contribute to Voat, either through submissions (they in some cases cannot submit links or start discussions whatsoever), or through comments (max of ten per day).

Now of course people can create alternate accounts to get around this, but I think we all recognize that that is not the important point.

On some level I feel as if I already knew this was the case; I recognize that this system helps combat spam and shillbots who attempt to flood Voat with the same links or rhetoric. This kind of spamming always gets downvoted, and so those accounts will accrue negative CCP and thus be unable to continue with their spamming.

However I want to make this post to get as much of us as possible thinking about what this really means.

Voat and its userbase is fundamentally pro-Freedom of Speech. That's why I am here, and I'm willing to bet that's why you are here. Our dedication to freedom of all forms it what distinguishes us from virtually every other website on the internet, and so I think it is clear why we should try to maintain this dedication no matter what.

Brushing aside the effect this system has on shills and spammers, I want to draw your attention to the effect this system could easily have on an ordinary person whose views happen to conflict with the general opinion on this website. I'm talking about people who maintain certain political, philosophical, religious, or any other kind of belief and opinion; people who can support these beliefs and will willingly state these beliefs loudly and for all to hear. People who don't just post unsubstantiated claims, but people who simply, in general, disagree with the Voat userbase on a plethora of issues.

Consider such a person. Now recognize how often, while browsing Voat, you have witnessed obvious cases of downvoting based on opinion. I'm talking about the disagree vote.

If such a person as we are considering experiences enough of these disagree votes over a long enough time, they could very easily accumulate negative CCP and find themselves unable to submit content or post as many comments as they like. Simply because they held different opinions than most of us.

Think about that.

This means that Voat, as it currently exists, fails to stand for free speech in this one way. It grants the majority the ability to silence minorities.

Does that sound familiar?

I did not come to Voat to find an echo chamber that would bounce my views off the walls and reinforce my beliefs. In fact, when I first arrived here almost one and a half years ago, I found quite the opposite. I was left-leaning politically and based many of my beliefs--without really realizing it--on my emotions, on what felt right, or what seemed virtuous. In my time here I have been able to reconnect with my more rational and fact-dependent self, but this would not have been possible if the rational arguments that in many cases persuaded me had been censored.

If we as a userbase begin to censor views unlike our own, we have only become what we hated to begin with. I know there are a lot of views that are so ridden with logical fallacies, unsubstantiated claims, and insupportable beliefs that they are almost painful to listen to...but there are also views that may or may not conflict with my own that do have substance, even if I disagree with them initially. It is incredibly important that we do not censor dissent of any form.

I was awakened to this reality by user @p0ssum, after whom the phenomenon in this submission title is named. I have not looked through his posting history, so I do not know what led him to go from having thousands of CCP to negative CCP--he may have been spamming, for instance, or attempting to incite violence, but I do not believe this is the case and I'm sure if I looked thoroughly through his comments I would not find evidence of either of these things. He may even have simply posted emotion-based, fact-ignoring, mental gymnastic-type mental mucus in terms of thoughts and opinions, but even that is not grounds for censorship. Based on what few posts of his I do recall having seen downvoted first-hand, I think his only crime is, primarily, holding left-wing opinions on a predominantly right-wing site.

This is not grounds for censorship, and I know you all recognize this.

I usually don't TL;DR, but:

TL;DR: Hypothetical users who post opinions that conflict with the general sentiment here on Voat, who then receive a great deal of disagree downvotes, have the potential of being disagreed with so often that their CCP becomes negative, and they find themselves unable to post submissions, and find themselves only able to comment a finite number of times each day. This is much more extreme than our, I think, reasonable CCP requirements for voting, as this is blatant censorship, by the community, of certain opinions. This goes completely against what Voat stands for.

I call out to the community to discuss this very critical topic, as I think it is important toward preserving Voat's integrity and philosophy. Am I wrong? Have I failed to consider something? Can someone persuade me this is somehow acceptable, that this is not censorship? If you can, please do.

Finally, I call out to the admins, @Atko and @PuttItOut, whom I respect tremendously, to weigh in on this issue.

Thank you.
